1	# Fused-megakernel component contract (portability spec)
2	
3	Owner requirement (2026-06-09): every (model × optimizer × arch) configuration —
4	all 3 models × 11 optimizers — composes into ONE persistent megakernel binary,
5	and the building blocks are **individually portable**: a third project lifts the
6	headers and instantiates a fused trainer without dragging this repo along. The
7	meta-programming lives in headers; the dispatch layer is generated and is the
8	only composition seam.
9	
10	## Component taxonomy (header-only, self-contained)
11	
12	| component | header(s) | contract |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| **Substrate** | `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` | `PersistentContext` (task counter, grid barrier, generation), one-CTA-per-SM persistent launch idiom. Depends on CUDA runtime only. |
15	| **Optimizer math** | `csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h` (×11) | Pure per-element apply math (`<opt>_step(...)`), no CUDA dependencies beyond `__device__` qualifiers, no state allocation, no I/O. Single source of truth — everything else `#include`s these (enforced by `scripts/check_math_single_source.py`). Already portable as-is. |
16	| **Optimizer tails** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh` | `apply_optimizer<OptId>(FusedOptState&, FusedScalars const&, ...)` — templates composing the algorithm headers into megakernel stages. Consumes the documented POD structs only. |
17	| **Model stages** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stage_<model>.cuh` (decoder / vit / mamba3 — ONE HEADER PER MODEL, not a monolith) | Provides `model_<m>_forward_stage<Dims>` and `model_<m>_backward_stage<Dims>`: batch-slice-local fwd/bwd with all activations CTA-local, writing per-CTA weight-grad partials to a caller-provided workspace. Templated on compile-time dims (d_model, n_layers, n_heads, seq, vocab). Includes ONLY the substrate header + CUDA. No globals, no repo build flags (every `SG_TUNED_*` consumed via `#ifndef` defaults). |
18	| **Composition** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh` | `launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, Tier>` — stage pipeline: fwd → bwd → grid barrier → deterministic weight-grad reduction → optimizer tail. The only place stages and tails meet. |
19	| **Cells** | `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu` (×33) | GENERATED 36-line instantiations (`megakernel_codegen.py`). Never hand-edited. |
20	| **Dispatch** | `csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp` + generated `fused_wired_cells.inc` / `fused_dispatch_table.inc` | `(model, optimizer, arch) → cell` routing. Generated from the same enumeration as the cells, so it cannot drift. Loud-gated: unwired/unready cells throw, never silently degrade. |
21	
22	## Portability rules (apply to every new/edited component)
23	1. **Self-containment**: a component header compiles with `#include <cuda_runtime.h>`
24	   + its declared includes only. Include-what-you-use; no transitive reliance.
25	2. **No hidden state**: no globals, no statics with side effects; all state flows
26	   through the documented POD structs (`PersistentContext`, `FusedOptState`,
27	   `FusedScalars`) or explicit pointers.
28	3. **Compile-time configuration only via documented template params or
29	   `#ifndef`-defaulted macros** (`SG_TUNED_*`); absent definitions must yield a
30	   correct (if untuned) kernel.
31	4. **The lift test**: copying `megakernel_common.cuh` + one `model_stage_*.cuh`
32	   + `opt_components.cuh` + the relevant `csrc/algorithms/*.h` into a fresh
33	   project and instantiating `launch_fused_megakernel<M,O,Tier>` must build and
34	   run. Each phase's validation includes compiling a minimal out-of-tree TU
35	   (tests/hw/test_component_portability.cu) that includes ONLY those headers.
36	5. **Generated artifacts are never edited by hand** — change the generator,
37	   regenerate everything, `git diff` must be generator-consistent.
38	6. **No placeholder math** on any wired path (owner no-suppression directive);
39	   surrogate stages exist only behind explicit unreadiness gates and throw at
40	   dispatch.
41	
42	## Phase status
43	- Phase 1 (in flight): real decoder fwd+bwd stages, validated vs eager — lands
44	  in `model_stages.cuh`, then is split per-model per this contract.
45	- Phase 2: vit + mamba3 stage headers (built against this contract natively).
46	- Phase 3: optimizer precompute stages in-kernel for the 9 non-trivial tails;
47	  SuperGrok2's CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU meta as in-kernel stages (the full
48	  "vit×sg2 in one binary").
49

1	"""tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py — runnable PyTorch ORACLE for the real decoder
2	forward+backward that the L3-REAL megakernel transcribes.
3	
4	WHY THIS EXISTS (the rigor substitute for an un-compilable, un-runnable .cu):
5	  PHASE 1 replaces the surrogate model stage in the persistent megakernel with
6	  the REAL transformer-decoder fwd+bwd. That CUDA backward is hand-derived and
7	  the implementing agent cannot compile or run it. So we first write the SAME
8	  fwd+bwd here in plain PyTorch using ONLY primitive ops — and a MANUAL backward
9	  (NO autograd) — then assert it matches torch.autograd's loss and every
10	  parameter .grad to ~1e-6. The CUDA megakernel is then ported line-for-line from
11	  this verified reference, converting "is my hand-derived backward correct?"
12	  (unrunnable) into "does my manual Python match autograd?" (runnable now).
13	
14	  This module is ALSO the per-tensor expected-grad oracle the parity test
15	  (tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py, item 5a) consumes: same init, same
16	  batch → expected loss + expected grads to compare the megakernel against.
17	
18	EXACT ARCHITECTURE TRANSCRIBED (grokking_race_v2.py, _raw_model → Transformer):
19	  Transformer(nl=2, d=128, h=4, ntok=99, seq=4)  [_raw_model hardcodes seq=4]
20	    tok = Embedding(99, 128)            # grokking_race_v2.py:360
21	    pos = Embedding(4, 128)             # seq=4 positions
22	    layers = 2 × DecoderBlock:          # :346-355
23	      attn = MultiheadAttention(128, 4, dropout=0, batch_first=True)  # :349
24	             causal mask = triu(ones(seq,seq), diagonal=1)            # :352
25	      n1, n2 = LayerNorm(128)           # :350  (eps=1e-5 default)
26	      ff = Linear(128,512) → GELU → Linear(512,128)   # :351 (GELU = exact erf)
27	      forward: a,_ = attn(x,x,x, attn_mask=causal)    # :354
28	               x = n1(x + a)                          # :355 POST-LN
29	               return n2(x + ff(x))                   # :355 POST-LN
30	    norm = LayerNorm(128)              # :362  final LN
31	    out  = Linear(128, 99)            # :362  head → 99 logits
32	    forward: h = tok(x) + pos(pos_ids)                # :366
33	             for l in layers: h = l(h)                # :367
34	             return out(norm(h)[:, -1, :])            # :368  LAST token only
35	  Loss: F.cross_entropy(m(tx), ty)  (mean over batch; grokking_race_v2.py:745)
36	
37	  nn.MultiheadAttention internals (verified bit-identical to the manual form in
38	  this file, max|diff|==0): in_proj_weight [3d, d] packs [Wq; Wk; Wv] row-blocks,
39	  in_proj_bias [3d]; qkv = x @ W_in^T + b_in then split into q,k,v each [.,.,d];
40	  per-head dh = d/h = 32; scores = (qh @ kh^T)/sqrt(dh); causal-masked (-inf on
41	  j>i); softmax over the key axis; ctx = attn @ vh; merge heads; out = ctx @
42	  W_out^T + b_out  (out_proj.weight [d,d], out_proj.bias [d]).
43	
44	NUMERICS (each verified against autograd here, and the values the CUDA must use):
45	  * GELU = EXACT erf: 0.5*x*(1+erf(x/sqrt2)); derivative
46	    0.5*(1+erf(x/sqrt2)) + x * (1/sqrt(2*pi)) * exp(-x^2/2).
47	    (The surrogate's tanh approximation differs by ~4e-4 — blows the 1e-4 grad
48	    tolerance — so it is WRONG for this path.)
49	  * LayerNorm eps = 1e-5 (torch default). Backward dx uses the two
50	    mean-correction terms (see _layernorm_backward).
51	  * Attention softmax subtracts the row max for stability (matches torch).
52	  * CrossEntropy is MEAN over B: dlogits = (softmax - onehot) / B.
53	
54	This file imports torch only; it needs NO GPU and NO built extension.
55	"""
56	
57	from __future__ import annotations
58	
59	import math
60	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
61	from typing import Dict, List, Tuple
62	
63	import torch
64	
65	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
66	# Architecture constants (single source — mirrored by the C++ layout header and
67	# the codegen). These are the decoder cell's fixed shapes in the grokking race.
68	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
69	VOCAB = 99      # num_tokens (DEFAULT_CONFIG["num_tokens"]) — token range [0,98]
70	D_MODEL = 128   # dim_model (MODEL_SCALES["small"])
71	N_HEADS = 4     # num_heads
72	N_LAYERS = 2    # num_layers
73	SEQ = 4         # _raw_model hardcodes seq=4 for the decoder (make_data → 4 toks)
74	D_FF = 4 * D_MODEL  # 512 — ff hidden (Linear(d,4*d))
75	D_HEAD = D_MODEL // N_HEADS  # 32
76	LN_EPS = 1e-5   # torch.nn.LayerNorm default eps
77	ATTN_SCALE = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D_HEAD)  # 1/sqrt(32)
78	
79	
80	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	# Exact-erf GELU and its derivative (the REAL nn.GELU(), NOT the tanh approx).
82	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
83	_INV_SQRT2 = 1.0 / math.sqrt(2.0)
84	_INV_SQRT_2PI = 1.0 / math.sqrt(2.0 * math.pi)
85	
86	
87	def gelu(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
88	    return 0.5 * x * (1.0 + torch.erf(x * _INV_SQRT2))
89	
90	
91	def gelu_grad(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
92	    # d/dx [0.5 x (1+erf(x/sqrt2))] = 0.5(1+erf(x/sqrt2)) + x * phi(x),
93	    # phi(x) = (1/sqrt(2pi)) exp(-x^2/2)  (the normal pdf).
94	    cdf = 0.5 * (1.0 + torch.erf(x * _INV_SQRT2))
95	    pdf = _INV_SQRT_2PI * torch.exp(-0.5 * x * x)
96	    return cdf + x * pdf
97	
98	
99	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	# LayerNorm fwd/bwd (eps=1e-5), over the last dim (size d). Affine (gamma,beta).
101	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102	def layernorm_forward(x, gamma, beta, eps=LN_EPS):
103	    """x: [..., d]. Returns (y, cache) where cache has the bwd intermediates."""
104	    mu = x.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
105	    xc = x - mu
106	    var = (xc * xc).mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
107	    inv_std = 1.0 / torch.sqrt(var + eps)
108	    xhat = xc * inv_std
109	    y = xhat * gamma + beta
110	    return y, (xhat, inv_std, gamma)
111	
112	
113	def layernorm_backward(dy, cache):
114	    """Returns (dx, dgamma, dbeta). dgamma/dbeta summed over all but last dim."""
115	    xhat, inv_std, gamma = cache
116	    d = xhat.shape[-1]
117	    # Reduce gamma/beta grads over every leading (batch/seq) axis.
118	    reduce_axes = tuple(range(dy.dim() - 1))
119	    dbeta = dy.sum(dim=reduce_axes)
120	    dgamma = (dy * xhat).sum(dim=reduce_axes)
121	    dxhat = dy * gamma
122	    # Standard LN dx: (1/d) * inv_std * (d*dxhat - sum(dxhat) - xhat*sum(dxhat*xhat))
123	    sum_dxhat = dxhat.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
124	    sum_dxhat_xhat = (dxhat * xhat).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
125	    dx = inv_std * (dxhat - (sum_dxhat + xhat * sum_dxhat_xhat) / d)
126	    return dx, dgamma, dbeta
127	
128	
129	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
130	# Softmax over the last dim with row-max subtraction (matches torch), + bwd.
131	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
132	def softmax_lastdim(x):
133	    m = x.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
134	    e = torch.exp(x - m)
135	    s = e.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
136	    return e / s
137	
138	
139	def softmax_backward(dy, y):
140	    # dx = y * (dy - sum(dy*y))  (over the softmax axis).
141	    s = (dy * y).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
142	    return y * (dy - s)
143	
144	
145	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
146	# Parameter container — mirrors named_parameters() ORDER exactly (30 tensors).
147	# The CUDA flat-buffer offsets are generated from this same order (see
148	# decoder_param_layout()).
149	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
150	# (name, shape) in the EXACT order torch's named_parameters() yields them. This
151	# is THE single source of truth for the flat weight layout; the C++ header
152	# (csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_layout.cuh) static-asserts the count + total.
153	def decoder_param_spec() -> List[Tuple[str, Tuple[int, ...]]]:
154	    spec: List[Tuple[str, Tuple[int, ...]]] = [
155	        ("tok.weight", (VOCAB, D_MODEL)),
156	        ("pos.weight", (SEQ, D_MODEL)),
157	    ]
158	    for li in range(N_LAYERS):
159	        p = f"layers.{li}."
160	        spec += [
161	            (p + "attn.in_proj_weight", (3 * D_MODEL, D_MODEL)),
162	            (p + "attn.in_proj_bias", (3 * D_MODEL,)),
163	            (p + "attn.out_proj.weight", (D_MODEL, D_MODEL)),
164	            (p + "attn.out_proj.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
165	            (p + "n1.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
166	            (p + "n1.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
167	            (p + "n2.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
168	            (p + "n2.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
169	            (p + "ff.0.weight", (D_FF, D_MODEL)),
170	            (p + "ff.0.bias", (D_FF,)),
171	            (p + "ff.2.weight", (D_MODEL, D_FF)),
172	            (p + "ff.2.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
173	        ]
174	    spec += [
175	        ("norm.weight", (D_MODEL,)),
176	        ("norm.bias", (D_MODEL,)),
177	        ("out.weight", (VOCAB, D_MODEL)),
178	        ("out.bias", (VOCAB,)),
179	    ]
180	    return spec
181	
182	
183	def decoder_param_layout() -> Dict[str, object]:
184	    """Flat-buffer layout: offsets/sizes per tensor (the megakernel ABI view).
185	
186	    Returns dict with: names, offsets (elements into the flat buffer), sizes,
187	    total (== 422755), n_tensors (== 30). The offsets follow named_parameters()
188	    order so the flat blob == torch.cat([p.reshape(-1) for _, p in
189	    model.named_parameters()]).
190	    """
191	    spec = decoder_param_spec()
192	    names, offsets, sizes = [], [], []
193	    off = 0
194	    for name, shape in spec:
195	        n = 1
196	        for s in shape:
197	            n *= s
198	        names.append(name)
199	        offsets.append(off)
200	        sizes.append(n)
201	        off += n
202	    return dict(names=names, offsets=offsets, sizes=sizes, shapes=[s for _, s in spec],
203	                total=off, n_tensors=len(spec))
204	
205	
206	@dataclass
207	class DecoderWeights:
208	    """All 30 decoder weights as named tensors. Built either from a flat buffer
209	    (the megakernel view) or from a torch nn module's named_parameters()."""
210	    tok: torch.Tensor
211	    pos: torch.Tensor
212	    layers: List[Dict[str, torch.Tensor]]
213	    norm_w: torch.Tensor
214	    norm_b: torch.Tensor
215	    out_w: torch.Tensor
216	    out_b: torch.Tensor
217	
218	    @staticmethod
219	    def from_named(named: Dict[str, torch.Tensor]) -> "DecoderWeights":
220	        layers = []
221	        for li in range(N_LAYERS):
222	            p = f"layers.{li}."
223	            layers.append(dict(
224	                in_w=named[p + "attn.in_proj_weight"],
225	                in_b=named[p + "attn.in_proj_bias"],
226	                out_w=named[p + "attn.out_proj.weight"],
227	                out_b=named[p + "attn.out_proj.bias"],
228	                n1_w=named[p + "n1.weight"], n1_b=named[p + "n1.bias"],
229	                n2_w=named[p + "n2.weight"], n2_b=named[p + "n2.bias"],
230	                ff0_w=named[p + "ff.0.weight"], ff0_b=named[p + "ff.0.bias"],
231	                ff2_w=named[p + "ff.2.weight"], ff2_b=named[p + "ff.2.bias"],
232	            ))
233	        return DecoderWeights(
234	            tok=named["tok.weight"], pos=named["pos.weight"], layers=layers,
235	            norm_w=named["norm.weight"], norm_b=named["norm.bias"],
236	            out_w=named["out.weight"], out_b=named["out.bias"])
237	
238	    @staticmethod
239	    def from_flat(flat: torch.Tensor) -> "DecoderWeights":
240	        lay = decoder_param_layout()
241	        named = {}
242	        for name, off, sz, shape in zip(lay["names"], lay["offsets"],
243	                                        lay["sizes"], lay["shapes"]):
244	            named[name] = flat[off:off + sz].reshape(shape)
245	        return DecoderWeights.from_named(named)
246	
247	
248	def _causal_mask(seq: int, device, dtype) -> torch.Tensor:
249	    """Additive mask [seq, seq]: 0 where j<=i, -inf where j>i (triu diag=1)."""
250	    m = torch.triu(torch.ones(seq, seq, dtype=torch.bool, device=device), 1)
251	    add = torch.zeros(seq, seq, device=device, dtype=dtype)
252	    add = add.masked_fill(m, float("-inf"))
253	    return add
254	
255	
256	# ===========================================================================
257	#  FORWARD (manual, primitive ops) — caches everything the manual backward needs.
258	# ===========================================================================
259	def decoder_forward(W: DecoderWeights, tokens: torch.Tensor,
260	                    targets: torch.Tensor):
261	    """tokens: [B, SEQ] int64 in [0, VOCAB). targets: [B] int64.
262	
263	    Returns (loss_scalar, cache). loss = mean-over-batch cross-entropy on the
264	    LAST-position logits. cache holds every fwd intermediate for the backward.
265	    """
266	    B, S = tokens.shape
267	    device, dtype = W.tok.device, W.tok.dtype
268	    add_mask = _causal_mask(S, device, dtype)  # [S,S]
269	
270	    # Embedding + positional. pos_ids = arange(S).
271	    pos_ids = torch.arange(S, device=device)
272	    h = W.tok[tokens] + W.pos[pos_ids].unsqueeze(0)   # [B,S,d]
273	
274	    layer_caches = []
275	    for li in range(N_LAYERS):
276	        L = W.layers[li]
277	        x_in = h  # residual base for the attention sublayer
278	        # ----- self-attention (MultiheadAttention semantics) -----
279	        qkv = x_in @ L["in_w"].t() + L["in_b"]        # [B,S,3d]
280	        q, k, v = qkv.split(D_MODEL, dim=-1)
281	        # split heads: [B,S,d] -> [B,h,S,dh]
282	        def sh(t):
283	            return t.reshape(B, S, N_HEADS, D_HEAD).permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
284	        qh, kh, vh = sh(q), sh(k), sh(v)
285	        scores = (qh @ kh.transpose(-2, -1)) * ATTN_SCALE   # [B,h,S,S]
286	        scores = scores + add_mask                          # causal
287	        attn = softmax_lastdim(scores)                      # [B,h,S,S]
288	        ctxh = attn @ vh                                     # [B,h,S,dh]
289	        ctx = ctxh.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, S, D_MODEL)  # merge heads
290	        a = ctx @ L["out_w"].t() + L["out_b"]               # [B,S,d]
291	        # ----- residual + n1 (POST-LN): x = n1(x_in + a) -----
292	        r1 = x_in + a
293	        x1, ln1_cache = layernorm_forward(r1, L["n1_w"], L["n1_b"])
294	        # ----- FFN: ff2(gelu(ff0(x1))) -----
295	        ff0 = x1 @ L["ff0_w"].t() + L["ff0_b"]              # [B,S,4d]
296	        g = gelu(ff0)                                        # [B,S,4d]
297	        ff2 = g @ L["ff2_w"].t() + L["ff2_b"]              # [B,S,d]
298	        # ----- residual + n2 (POST-LN): h = n2(x1 + ff2) -----
299	        r2 = x1 + ff2
300	        h2, ln2_cache = layernorm_forward(r2, L["n2_w"], L["n2_b"])
301	        layer_caches.append(dict(
302	            x_in=x_in, qkv=qkv, qh=qh, kh=kh, vh=vh, attn=attn, ctxh=ctxh,
303	            ctx=ctx, r1=r1, x1=x1, ln1_cache=ln1_cache, ff0=ff0, g=g, r2=r2,
304	            ln2_cache=ln2_cache))
305	        h = h2
306	
307	    # Final norm + head on the LAST position only.
308	    h_last = h[:, -1, :]                                   # [B,d]
309	    hn, norm_cache = layernorm_forward(h_last, W.norm_w, W.norm_b)
310	    logits = hn @ W.out_w.t() + W.out_b                    # [B,VOCAB]
311	    # Cross-entropy, mean over batch (numerically-stable log-softmax).
312	    m = logits.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
313	    logz = m.squeeze(-1) + torch.log(torch.exp(logits - m).sum(dim=-1))
314	    nll = logz - logits.gather(1, targets.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1)
315	    loss = nll.mean()
316	    cache = dict(B=B, S=S, tokens=tokens, targets=targets,
317	                 layer_caches=layer_caches, h_last=h_last, hn=hn,
318	                 norm_cache=norm_cache, logits=logits, add_mask=add_mask)
319	    return loss, cache
320	
321	
322	# ===========================================================================
323	#  BACKWARD (manual, NO autograd) — returns grads for every named parameter.
324	# ===========================================================================
325	def decoder_backward(W: DecoderWeights, cache) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
326	    B, S = cache["B"], cache["S"]
327	    targets = cache["targets"]
328	    tokens = cache["tokens"]
329	    grads: Dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
330	
331	    # ----- CE backward: dlogits = (softmax - onehot) / B -----
332	    logits = cache["logits"]
333	    sm = softmax_lastdim(logits)                           # [B,VOCAB]
334	    onehot = torch.zeros_like(sm)
335	    onehot.scatter_(1, targets.unsqueeze(1), 1.0)
336	    dlogits = (sm - onehot) / B                            # [B,VOCAB]
337	
338	    # ----- head (out): logits = hn @ out_w^T + out_b -----
339	    hn = cache["hn"]                                       # [B,d]
340	    grads["out.weight"] = dlogits.t() @ hn                 # [VOCAB,d]
341	    grads["out.bias"] = dlogits.sum(dim=0)                 # [VOCAB]
342	    dhn = dlogits @ W.out_w                                # [B,d]
343	
344	    # ----- final norm backward -----
345	    dh_last, dnorm_w, dnorm_b = layernorm_backward(dhn, cache["norm_cache"])
346	    grads["norm.weight"] = dnorm_w
347	    grads["norm.bias"] = dnorm_b
348	
349	    # Upstream into the last layer's output: only the LAST position has grad.
350	    dh = torch.zeros(B, S, D_MODEL, device=hn.device, dtype=hn.dtype)
351	    dh[:, -1, :] = dh_last
352	
353	    # ----- per-layer backward (reverse) -----
354	    for li in reversed(range(N_LAYERS)):
355	        L = W.layers[li]
356	        lc = cache["layer_caches"][li]
357	        gp = f"layers.{li}."
358	        # h2 = n2(r2);  dh is grad wrt h2.
359	        dr2, dn2_w, dn2_b = layernorm_backward(dh, lc["ln2_cache"])
360	        grads[gp + "n2.weight"] = dn2_w
361	        grads[gp + "n2.bias"] = dn2_b
362	        # r2 = x1 + ff2  -> grad flows to x1 (residual) AND ff2.
363	        dff2 = dr2
364	        dx1 = dr2.clone()
365	        # ff2 = g @ ff2_w^T + ff2_b
366	        g = lc["g"]                                        # [B,S,4d]
367	        grads[gp + "ff.2.weight"] = (dff2.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).t()
368	                                     @ g.reshape(-1, D_FF))   # [d,4d]
369	        grads[gp + "ff.2.bias"] = dff2.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).sum(dim=0)
370	        dg = dff2 @ W.layers[li]["ff2_w"]                  # [B,S,4d]
371	        # gelu backward
372	        dff0 = dg * gelu_grad(lc["ff0"])                   # [B,S,4d]
373	        # ff0 = x1 @ ff0_w^T + ff0_b
374	        x1 = lc["x1"]
375	        grads[gp + "ff.0.weight"] = (dff0.reshape(-1, D_FF).t()
376	                                     @ x1.reshape(-1, D_MODEL))  # [4d,d]
377	        grads[gp + "ff.0.bias"] = dff0.reshape(-1, D_FF).sum(dim=0)
378	        dx1 = dx1 + dff0 @ W.layers[li]["ff0_w"]           # add FFN path to x1
379	        # x1 = n1(r1) -> backward
380	        dr1, dn1_w, dn1_b = layernorm_backward(dx1, lc["ln1_cache"])
381	        grads[gp + "n1.weight"] = dn1_w
382	        grads[gp + "n1.bias"] = dn1_b
383	        # r1 = x_in + a -> grad to x_in (residual) AND a (attention out).
384	        da = dr1
385	        dx_in = dr1.clone()
386	        # a = ctx @ out_w^T + out_b
387	        ctx = lc["ctx"]                                    # [B,S,d]
388	        grads[gp + "attn.out_proj.weight"] = (da.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).t()
389	                                              @ ctx.reshape(-1, D_MODEL))
390	        grads[gp + "attn.out_proj.bias"] = da.reshape(-1, D_MODEL).sum(dim=0)
391	        dctx = da @ W.layers[li]["out_w"]                  # [B,S,d]
392	        # merge-heads backward: ctx[B,S,d] <- ctxh[B,h,S,dh]
393	        dctxh = dctx.reshape(B, S, N_HEADS, D_HEAD).permute(0, 2, 1, 3)  # [B,h,S,dh]
394	        # ctxh = attn @ vh
395	        attn = lc["attn"]; vh = lc["vh"]; qh = lc["qh"]; kh = lc["kh"]
396	        dattn = dctxh @ vh.transpose(-2, -1)               # [B,h,S,S]
397	        dvh = attn.transpose(-2, -1) @ dctxh               # [B,h,S,dh]
398	        # softmax backward (over key axis) — masked positions had attn==0 so
399	        # their dscore contribution is zero (y*(...)==0), matching the -inf fwd.
400	        dscores = softmax_backward(dattn, attn)            # [B,h,S,S]
401	        dscores = dscores * ATTN_SCALE
402	        # scores = qh @ kh^T
403	        dqh = dscores @ kh                                 # [B,h,S,dh]
404	        dkh = dscores.transpose(-2, -1) @ qh               # [B,h,S,dh]
405	        # un-split heads: [B,h,S,dh] -> [B,S,d]
406	        def mh(t):
407	            return t.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(B, S, D_MODEL)
408	        dq, dk, dv = mh(dqh), mh(dkh), mh(dvh)             # each [B,S,d]
409	        dqkv = torch.cat([dq, dk, dv], dim=-1)             # [B,S,3d]
410	        # qkv = x_in @ in_w^T + in_b
411	        x_in = lc["x_in"]
412	        grads[gp + "attn.in_proj_weight"] = (dqkv.reshape(-1, 3 * D_MODEL).t()
413	                                             @ x_in.reshape(-1, D_MODEL))
414	        grads[gp + "attn.in_proj_bias"] = dqkv.reshape(-1, 3 * D_MODEL).sum(dim=0)
415	        dx_in = dx_in + dqkv @ W.layers[li]["in_w"]        # add attention path
416	        # propagate to the previous layer's output (or the embedding).
417	        dh = dx_in
418	
419	    # ----- embedding backward: h0 = tok[tokens] + pos[pos_ids] -----
420	    # dh is grad wrt h0 [B,S,d]. tok grad scatter-adds per token id; pos grad
421	    # sums over batch per position.
422	    dtok = torch.zeros_like(W.tok)                         # [VOCAB,d]
423	    # index_add_ accumulates duplicate token ids deterministically enough for the
424	    # reference; the CUDA path uses a fixed-order accumulation (see report).
425	    dtok.index_add_(0, tokens.reshape(-1), dh.reshape(-1, D_MODEL))
426	    grads["tok.weight"] = dtok
427	    grads["pos.weight"] = dh.sum(dim=0)                    # [S,d]
428	    return grads
429

431	# ===========================================================================
432	#  Convenience: full step on a torch nn.Module's params (for the parity test).
433	# ===========================================================================
434	def oracle_loss_and_grads(named_params: Dict[str, torch.Tensor],
435	                          tokens: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor):
436	    """Run the manual fwd+bwd over a dict of named parameter tensors.
437	
438	    Returns (loss_float, grads_named). The named_params dict must contain the 30
439	    decoder tensors (same keys as named_parameters()). All compute is in the
440	    dtype of the params (use fp32 for the correctness baseline)."""
441	    W = DecoderWeights.from_named(named_params)
442	    loss, cache = decoder_forward(W, tokens, targets)
443	    grads = decoder_backward(W, cache)
444	    return loss.item(), grads

1	"""tests/hw/decoder_kernel_mirror.py — single-threaded STRUCTURAL mirror of the
2	CUDA decoder megakernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages_decoder.cuh).
3	
4	WHY (the gate the math-oracle cannot provide): decoder_oracle.py proves the
5	decoder fwd/bwd MATH is correct (matched to autograd ~1e-15). It does NOT
6	exercise the CUDA kernel's *structure* — the smem buffer reuse/aliasing, the
7	recompute-in-backward, the head-split index arithmetic, the owner-thread grad
8	accumulation, the per-sample sequential reduction. That structure is exactly
9	where a hand-written, un-runnable backward hides missing terms / index bugs /
10	dead-buffer reads (e.g. an attention dv term computed from an already-overwritten
11	softmax weight).
12	
13	This module re-implements the kernel ALGORITHM in plain Python — same buffers
14	(as numpy/torch arrays), same aliasing decisions, same loop nests and index math,
15	same per-sample sequential weight-grad accumulation into a CTA-style partial — so
16	that asserting it against decoder_oracle's grads (~1e-6 on a tiny batch) catches
17	the STRUCTURAL bug class. It is single-threaded, so it does NOT catch
18	__syncthreads races (those are verified by reading each sync against the buffer it
19	guards — see the kernel header comments); it DOES catch everything else.
20	
21	The mirror follows the .cuh line-by-line: dec_forward_sample,
22	dec_recompute_layer, dec_backward_sample, dec_linear/_bwd, dec_layernorm_*,
23	and the three-pass attention backward (A: dv, B: dscores, C: dq/dk).
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import math
29	from typing import Dict
30	
31	import torch
32	
33	from tests.hw.decoder_oracle import (
34	    DecoderWeights, decoder_param_layout,
35	    VOCAB, D_MODEL, N_HEADS, N_LAYERS, SEQ, D_FF, D_HEAD, LN_EPS, ATTN_SCALE,
36	    gelu, gelu_grad,
37	)
38	
39	_F64 = torch.float64  # mirror in fp64 so the only diff vs oracle is structure
40

42	# --- primitive ops, mirroring the .cuh device functions exactly --------------
43	def _linear(x, W, b, in_dim, out_dim):
44	    # y[s,o] = sum_k x[s,k]*W[o,k] + b[o]   (W row-major [out,in])
45	    y = torch.zeros(SEQ, out_dim, dtype=_F64)
46	    for s in range(SEQ):
47	        for o in range(out_dim):
48	            acc = b[o].item() if b is not None else 0.0
49	            for k in range(in_dim):
50	                acc += x[s, k].item() * W[o, k].item()
51	            y[s, o] = acc
52	    return y
53	
54	
55	def _layernorm_fwd(x, gamma, beta):
56	    y = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
57	    xhat = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
58	    inv = torch.zeros(SEQ, dtype=_F64)
59	    for s in range(SEQ):
60	        mean = x[s].mean()
61	        var = ((x[s] - mean) ** 2).mean()
62	        i = 1.0 / math.sqrt(var.item() + LN_EPS)
63	        inv[s] = i
64	        for j in range(D_MODEL):
65	            xh = (x[s, j] - mean) * i
66	            xhat[s, j] = xh
67	            y[s, j] = xh * gamma[j] + beta[j]
68	    return y, xhat, inv

71	# --- the per-sample forward (mirrors dec_forward_sample) ----------------------
72	def _forward_sample(W: DecoderWeights, tokens_s, target):
73	    sm = {}
74	    # embedding + pos -> layer_in[0]
75	    h = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
76	    for s in range(SEQ):
77	        for j in range(D_MODEL):
78	            h[s, j] = W.tok[tokens_s[s], j] + W.pos[s, j]
79	    sm["layer_in"] = [h.clone(), None]
80	    for li in range(N_LAYERS):
81	        L = W.layers[li]
82	        hin = sm["layer_in"][li]
83	        qkv = _linear(hin, L["in_w"], L["in_b"], D_MODEL, 3 * D_MODEL)
84	        attn = torch.zeros(N_HEADS, SEQ, SEQ, dtype=_F64)
85	        ctx = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
86	        for hh in range(N_HEADS):
87	            qoff = hh * D_HEAD
88	            for qi in range(SEQ):
89	                sc = [(-math.inf) for _ in range(SEQ)]
90	                maxs = -math.inf
91	                for kj in range(SEQ):
92	                    if kj > qi:
93	                        continue
94	                    dot = 0.0
95	                    for t in range(D_HEAD):
96	                        dot += qkv[qi, qoff + t].item() * qkv[kj, D_MODEL + qoff + t].item()
97	                    sc[kj] = dot * ATTN_SCALE
98	                    maxs = max(maxs, sc[kj])
99	                denom = 0.0
100	                for kj in range(SEQ):
101	                    e = math.exp(sc[kj] - maxs) if kj <= qi else 0.0
102	                    sc[kj] = e
103	                    denom += e
104	                for kj in range(SEQ):
105	                    attn[hh, qi, kj] = sc[kj] / denom
106	                for t in range(D_HEAD):
107	                    acc = 0.0
108	                    for kj in range(qi + 1):
109	                        acc += attn[hh, qi, kj].item() * qkv[kj, 2 * D_MODEL + qoff + t].item()
110	                    ctx[qi, qoff + t] = acc
111	        a = _linear(ctx, L["out_w"], L["out_b"], D_MODEL, D_MODEL)
112	        r1 = hin + a
113	        x1, n1_xhat, n1_inv = _layernorm_fwd(r1, L["n1_w"], L["n1_b"])
114	        ff0 = _linear(x1, L["ff0_w"], L["ff0_b"], D_MODEL, D_FF)
115	        gact = gelu(ff0)
116	        ff2 = _linear(gact, L["ff2_w"], L["ff2_b"], D_FF, D_MODEL)
117	        r2 = x1 + ff2
118	        h2, n2_xhat, n2_inv = _layernorm_fwd(r2, L["n2_w"], L["n2_b"])
119	        sm[f"L{li}"] = dict(qkv=qkv, attn=attn, ctx=ctx, x1=x1, ff0=ff0,
120	                            gact=gact, n1_xhat=n1_xhat, n1_inv=n1_inv,
121	                            n2_xhat=n2_xhat, n2_inv=n2_inv)
122	        if li + 1 < N_LAYERS:
123	            sm["layer_in"][li + 1] = h2
124	        else:
125	            sm["final_in"] = h2
126	    # final norm (last pos) + head -> logits
127	    hlast = sm["final_in"][SEQ - 1]
128	    mean = hlast.mean()
129	    var = ((hlast - mean) ** 2).mean()
130	    inv = 1.0 / math.sqrt(var.item() + LN_EPS)
131	    fn_xhat = torch.zeros(D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
132	    hn = torch.zeros(D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
133	    for j in range(D_MODEL):
134	        xh = (hlast[j] - mean) * inv
135	        fn_xhat[j] = xh
136	        hn[j] = xh * W.norm_w[j] + W.norm_b[j]
137	    logits = torch.zeros(VOCAB, dtype=_F64)
138	    for o in range(VOCAB):
139	        acc = W.out_b[o].item()
140	        for k in range(D_MODEL):
141	            acc += hn[k].item() * W.out_w[o, k].item()
142	        logits[o] = acc
143	    sm["fn_xhat"] = fn_xhat
144	    sm["fn_inv"] = inv
145	    sm["logits"] = logits
146	    return sm

149	# --- recompute one layer's fwd intermediates (mirrors dec_recompute_layer) ----
150	def _recompute_layer(W, li, sm):
151	    """RE-RUN the layer forward from the cached layer INPUT (sm['layer_in'][li]),
152	    exactly as the CUDA dec_recompute_layer does (it does NOT reuse a per-layer
153	    cache — only layer_in survives). This exercises the recompute path's index
154	    math + that it reproduces the forward values; we assert it equals the original
155	    forward cache to catch a recompute divergence (e.g. a wrong residual or a
156	    clobbered input)."""
157	    L = W.layers[li]
158	    hin = sm["layer_in"][li]
159	    qkv = _linear(hin, L["in_w"], L["in_b"], D_MODEL, 3 * D_MODEL)
160	    attn = torch.zeros(N_HEADS, SEQ, SEQ, dtype=_F64)
161	    ctx = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
162	    for hh in range(N_HEADS):
163	        qoff = hh * D_HEAD
164	        for qi in range(SEQ):
165	            sc = [(-math.inf) for _ in range(SEQ)]
166	            maxs = -math.inf
167	            for kj in range(SEQ):
168	                if kj > qi:
169	                    continue
170	                dot = 0.0
171	                for t in range(D_HEAD):
172	                    dot += qkv[qi, qoff + t].item() * qkv[kj, D_MODEL + qoff + t].item()
173	                sc[kj] = dot * ATTN_SCALE
174	                maxs = max(maxs, sc[kj])
175	            denom = 0.0
176	            for kj in range(SEQ):
177	                e = math.exp(sc[kj] - maxs) if kj <= qi else 0.0
178	                sc[kj] = e
179	                denom += e
180	            for kj in range(SEQ):
181	                attn[hh, qi, kj] = sc[kj] / denom
182	            for t in range(D_HEAD):
183	                acc = 0.0
184	                for kj in range(qi + 1):
185	                    acc += attn[hh, qi, kj].item() * qkv[kj, 2 * D_MODEL + qoff + t].item()
186	                ctx[qi, qoff + t] = acc
187	    a = _linear(ctx, L["out_w"], L["out_b"], D_MODEL, D_MODEL)
188	    r1 = hin + a
189	    x1, n1_xhat, n1_inv = _layernorm_fwd(r1, L["n1_w"], L["n1_b"])
190	    ff0 = _linear(x1, L["ff0_w"], L["ff0_b"], D_MODEL, D_FF)
191	    gact = gelu(ff0)
192	    # n2 caches (xhat/inv) require r2; the CUDA recompute computes r2 into ctx and
193	    # runs LN fwd for the caches (output discarded).
194	    ff2 = _linear(gact, L["ff2_w"], L["ff2_b"], D_FF, D_MODEL)
195	    r2 = x1 + ff2
196	    _, n2_xhat, n2_inv = _layernorm_fwd(r2, L["n2_w"], L["n2_b"])
197	    rc = dict(qkv=qkv, attn=attn, ctx=ctx, x1=x1, ff0=ff0, gact=gact,
198	              n1_xhat=n1_xhat, n1_inv=n1_inv, n2_xhat=n2_xhat, n2_inv=n2_inv)
199	    # Recompute MUST reproduce the original forward exactly (same inputs/ops).
200	    orig = sm[f"L{li}"]
201	    for k in ("qkv", "ctx", "x1", "ff0", "gact", "n1_xhat", "n2_xhat"):
202	        d = (rc[k] - orig[k]).abs().max().item()
203	        assert d < 1e-9, f"recompute layer {li} field {k} diverged by {d:.2e}"
204	    return rc

207	# --- the per-sample backward (mirrors dec_backward_sample) --------------------
208	def _backward_sample(W: DecoderWeights, g: Dict[str, torch.Tensor],
209	                     tokens_s, target, B, sm):
210	    # CE backward: dlogits = (softmax - onehot)/B
211	    logits = sm["logits"]
212	    mx = logits.max().item()
213	    es = sum(math.exp(logits[o].item() - mx) for o in range(VOCAB))
214	    dlogits = torch.zeros(VOCAB, dtype=_F64)
215	    for o in range(VOCAB):
216	        smo = math.exp(logits[o].item() - mx) / es
217	        dlogits[o] = (smo - (1.0 if o == target else 0.0)) / B
218	    # head bwd: dW_out += dlogits ⊗ hn ; db_out += dlogits ; dhn = dlogits @ out_w
219	    fn_xhat = sm["fn_xhat"]
220	    hn = torch.zeros(D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
221	    for j in range(D_MODEL):
222	        hn[j] = fn_xhat[j] * W.norm_w[j] + W.norm_b[j]
223	    for o in range(VOCAB):
224	        g["out.bias"][o] += dlogits[o]
225	        for j in range(D_MODEL):
226	            g["out.weight"][o, j] += dlogits[o] * hn[j]
227	    dhn = torch.zeros(D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
228	    for j in range(D_MODEL):
229	        acc = 0.0
230	        for o in range(VOCAB):
231	            acc += dlogits[o].item() * W.out_w[o, j].item()
232	        dhn[j] = acc
233	    # final-norm bwd (single row = last position).
234	    dy = dhn
235	    for j in range(D_MODEL):
236	        g["norm.bias"][j] += dy[j]
237	        g["norm.weight"][j] += dy[j] * fn_xhat[j]
238	    sda = sum((dy[j] * W.norm_w[j]).item() for j in range(D_MODEL))
239	    sdax = sum((dy[j] * W.norm_w[j] * fn_xhat[j]).item() for j in range(D_MODEL))
240	    inv_s = sm["fn_inv"]
241	    dh = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
242	    for j in range(D_MODEL):
243	        dxhat = dy[j] * W.norm_w[j]
244	        dh[SEQ - 1, j] = inv_s * (dxhat - (sda + fn_xhat[j] * sdax) / D_MODEL)
245	    # per-layer backward (reverse)
246	    for li in reversed(range(N_LAYERS)):
247	        L = W.layers[li]
248	        gp = f"layers.{li}."
249	        c = _recompute_layer(W, li, sm)
250	        qkv, attn, ctx_fwd = c["qkv"], c["attn"], c["ctx"]
251	        x1, ff0, gact = c["x1"], c["ff0"], c["gact"]
252	        n1_xhat, n1_inv = c["n1_xhat"], c["n1_inv"]
253	        n2_xhat, n2_inv = c["n2_xhat"], c["n2_inv"]
254	        # n2 bwd: dh -> dr2 ; accumulate n2 gamma/beta.
255	        dr2 = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
256	        for j in range(D_MODEL):
257	            for s in range(SEQ):
258	                d = dh[s, j]
259	                g[gp + "n2.bias"][j] += d
260	                g[gp + "n2.weight"][j] += d * n2_xhat[s, j]
261	        for s in range(SEQ):
262	            sda = sum((dh[s, j] * L["n2_w"][j]).item() for j in range(D_MODEL))
263	            sdax = sum((dh[s, j] * L["n2_w"][j] * n2_xhat[s, j]).item()
264	                       for j in range(D_MODEL))
265	            for j in range(D_MODEL):
266	                dxhat = dh[s, j] * L["n2_w"][j]
267	                dr2[s, j] = n2_inv[s] * (dxhat - (sda + n2_xhat[s, j] * sdax) / D_MODEL)
268	        # dx1 := dr2 (residual). dff2 = dr2.
269	        dx1 = dr2.clone()
270	        # ff.2 bwd: dW += dr2^T @ gact ; db += sum dr2 ; dff0 = (dr2 @ ff2_w)*gelu'(ff0)
271	        for o in range(D_MODEL):
272	            for i in range(D_FF):
273	                acc = 0.0
274	                for s in range(SEQ):
275	                    acc += dr2[s, o].item() * gact[s, i].item()
276	                g[gp + "ff.2.weight"][o, i] += acc
277	            acc = 0.0
278	            for s in range(SEQ):
279	                acc += dr2[s, o].item()
280	            g[gp + "ff.2.bias"][o] += acc
281	        dff0 = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_FF, dtype=_F64)
282	        ggrad = gelu_grad(ff0)
283	        for s in range(SEQ):
284	            for i in range(D_FF):
285	                dg = 0.0
286	                for o in range(D_MODEL):
287	                    dg += dr2[s, o].item() * L["ff2_w"][o, i].item()
288	                dff0[s, i] = dg * ggrad[s, i]
289	        # ff.0 bwd: dW += dff0^T @ x1 ; db += sum dff0 ; dx1 += dff0 @ ff0_w
290	        for o in range(D_FF):
291	            for i in range(D_MODEL):
292	                acc = 0.0
293	                for s in range(SEQ):
294	                    acc += dff0[s, o].item() * x1[s, i].item()
295	                g[gp + "ff.0.weight"][o, i] += acc
296	            acc = 0.0
297	            for s in range(SEQ):
298	                acc += dff0[s, o].item()
299	            g[gp + "ff.0.bias"][o] += acc
300	        for s in range(SEQ):
301	            for i in range(D_MODEL):
302	                acc = 0.0
303	                for o in range(D_FF):
304	                    acc += dff0[s, o].item() * L["ff0_w"][o, i].item()
305	                dx1[s, i] += acc
306	        # n1 bwd: dx1 -> dr1 ; accumulate n1 gamma/beta.
307	        dr1 = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
308	        for j in range(D_MODEL):
309	            for s in range(SEQ):
310	                d = dx1[s, j]
311	                g[gp + "n1.bias"][j] += d
312	                g[gp + "n1.weight"][j] += d * n1_xhat[s, j]
313	        for s in range(SEQ):
314	            sda = sum((dx1[s, j] * L["n1_w"][j]).item() for j in range(D_MODEL))
315	            sdax = sum((dx1[s, j] * L["n1_w"][j] * n1_xhat[s, j]).item()
316	                       for j in range(D_MODEL))
317	            for j in range(D_MODEL):
318	                dxhat = dx1[s, j] * L["n1_w"][j]
319	                dr1[s, j] = n1_inv[s] * (dxhat - (sda + n1_xhat[s, j] * sdax) / D_MODEL)
320	        # r1 = x_in + a -> da = dr1 ; dx_in := dr1 (residual).
321	        da = dr1
322	        dx_in = dr1.clone()
323	        # out_proj bwd: dW += da^T @ ctx_fwd ; db += sum da ; dctx = da @ out_w
324	        for o in range(D_MODEL):
325	            for i in range(D_MODEL):
326	                acc = 0.0
327	                for s in range(SEQ):
328	                    acc += da[s, o].item() * ctx_fwd[s, i].item()
329	                g[gp + "attn.out_proj.weight"][o, i] += acc
330	            acc = 0.0
331	            for s in range(SEQ):
332	                acc += da[s, o].item()
333	            g[gp + "attn.out_proj.bias"][o] += acc
334	        dctx = torch.zeros(SEQ, D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
335	        for s in range(SEQ):
336	            for i in range(D_MODEL):
337	                acc = 0.0
338	                for o in range(D_MODEL):
339	                    acc += da[s, o].item() * L["out_w"][o, i].item()
340	                dctx[s, i] = acc
341	        # --- attention backward (3 passes: A dv, B dscores, C dq/dk) ---
342	        dqkv = torch.zeros(SEQ, 3 * D_MODEL, dtype=_F64)
343	        # A: dv[kj,qoff+t] = sum_{qi>=kj} attn[hh,qi,kj]*dctx[qi,qoff+t]
344	        for kj in range(SEQ):
345	            for hh in range(N_HEADS):
346	                qoff = hh * D_HEAD
347	                for t in range(D_HEAD):
348	                    acc = 0.0
349	                    for qi in range(kj, SEQ):
350	                        acc += attn[hh, qi, kj].item() * dctx[qi, qoff + t].item()
351	                    dqkv[kj, 2 * D_MODEL + qoff + t] = acc
352	        # B: dsc[hh,qi,kj] = attn*(datt - sum_k datt*attn)*scale
353	        dsc = torch.zeros(N_HEADS, SEQ, SEQ, dtype=_F64)
354	        for hh in range(N_HEADS):
355	            qoff = hh * D_HEAD
356	            for qi in range(SEQ):
357	                datt = [0.0] * SEQ
358	                for kj in range(qi + 1):
359	                    acc = 0.0
360	                    for t in range(D_HEAD):
361	                        acc += dctx[qi, qoff + t].item() * qkv[kj, 2 * D_MODEL + qoff + t].item()
362	                    datt[kj] = acc
363	                dot = 0.0
364	                for kj in range(qi + 1):
365	                    dot += datt[kj] * attn[hh, qi, kj].item()
366	                for kj in range(SEQ):
367	                    a = attn[hh, qi, kj].item()
368	                    dsc[hh, qi, kj] = (a * (datt[kj] - dot) * ATTN_SCALE) if kj <= qi else 0.0
369	        # C: dq[pos,qoff+t]=sum_kj dsc[hh,pos,kj]*k[kj]; dk[pos]=sum_qi dsc[hh,qi,pos]*q[qi]
370	        for pos in range(SEQ):
371	            for hh in range(N_HEADS):
372	                qoff = hh * D_HEAD
373	                for t in range(D_HEAD):
374	                    dq = 0.0
375	                    dk = 0.0
376	                    for kj in range(SEQ):
377	                        dq += dsc[hh, pos, kj].item() * qkv[kj, D_MODEL + qoff + t].item()
378	                        dk += dsc[hh, kj, pos].item() * qkv[kj, qoff + t].item()
379	                    dqkv[pos, qoff + t] = dq
380	                    dqkv[pos, D_MODEL + qoff + t] = dk
381	        # in_proj bwd: dW += dqkv^T @ x_in ; db += sum dqkv ; dx_in += dqkv @ in_w
382	        x_in = sm["layer_in"][li]
383	        for o in range(3 * D_MODEL):
384	            for i in range(D_MODEL):
385	                acc = 0.0
386	                for s in range(SEQ):
387	                    acc += dqkv[s, o].item() * x_in[s, i].item()
388	                g[gp + "attn.in_proj_weight"][o, i] += acc
389	            acc = 0.0
390	            for s in range(SEQ):
391	                acc += dqkv[s, o].item()
392	            g[gp + "attn.in_proj_bias"][o] += acc
393	        for s in range(SEQ):
394	            for i in range(D_MODEL):
395	                acc = 0.0
396	                for o in range(3 * D_MODEL):
397	                    acc += dqkv[s, o].item() * L["in_w"][o, i].item()
398	                dx_in[s, i] += acc
399	        dh = dx_in
400	    # embedding bwd: tok scatter-add per id (sequential positions), pos sum.
401	    for j in range(D_MODEL):
402	        for s in range(SEQ):
403	            d = dh[s, j]
404	            g["tok.weight"][tokens_s[s], j] += d
405	            g["pos.weight"][s, j] += d
406	
407	
408	def mirror_loss_and_grads(named_params: Dict[str, torch.Tensor],
409	                          tokens: torch.Tensor, targets: torch.Tensor):
410	    """Run the STRUCTURAL kernel mirror over the whole (small) batch.
411	
412	    Mirrors the CTA loop: per sample, forward then immediately backward,
413	    accumulating weight grads into one partial (here a single CTA == whole batch,
414	    which is what determinism requires per element). Returns (loss, grads)."""
415	    named = {k: v.to(_F64) for k, v in named_params.items()}
416	    W = DecoderWeights.from_named(named)
417	    lay = decoder_param_layout()
418	    g = {name: torch.zeros(shape, dtype=_F64)
419	         for name, shape in zip(lay["names"], lay["shapes"])}
420	    B = tokens.shape[0]
421	    nll_sum = 0.0
422	    for b in range(B):
423	        tok_s = [int(tokens[b, s]) for s in range(SEQ)]
424	        tgt = int(targets[b])
425	        sm = _forward_sample(W, tok_s, tgt)
426	        logits = sm["logits"]
427	        mx = logits.max().item()
428	        es = sum(math.exp(logits[o].item() - mx) for o in range(VOCAB))
429	        nll_sum += (mx + math.log(es)) - logits[tgt].item()
430	        _backward_sample(W, g, tok_s, tgt, B, sm)
431	    return nll_sum / B, g

1	# BUILD_AND_VALIDATE — lever (a): L1 fused megakernel in the grokking race
2	
3	This document is the operator runbook for the change that wires the L3-substrate
4	fused model×optimizer megakernels into the grokking race **as the optimizer
5	step**, with the FULL optimizer scalar set (no placeholder scalars). Run the
6	sequence below on a real **sm_90 (H100/H200)** device after the concurrent GPU
7	job releases the device and the live `_ops.so`.
8	
9	> Source-complete only. The implementing agent did NOT build, did NOT run any GPU
10	> validation, and did NOT touch `setup.py` / `compile.py` / `build.sh` / `README`
11	> (a sibling agent owns those). Everything below is for the operator to run.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 0. The one deviation you must know (read first)
16	
17	The directive's items 4–5 assume the L3 fused megakernel computes the **real**
18	model forward/backward (so a "megakernel-vs-eager loss-trajectory" test is
19	meaningful). **It does not.** The L3 model stages are an element-local
20	**surrogate** over the flat parameter blob:
21	
22	* `csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages.cuh`:
23	  `acts[gi] = GELU(params[gi] + input[gi])`, `grad[gi] = acts[gi]·GELU'(params[gi])`
24	  — no token embedding, no attention, no matmul, no cross-entropy.
25	* The race's model `input` is **int token indices** `[B, seq]`; the kernel wants
26	  `float[numel(params)]`. They are not even shape-compatible.
27	* On the L3 path the kernel does `(void)grad;` and recomputes its own surrogate
28	  grad, ignoring any real gradient handed in.
29	
30	Therefore an L3 cell's loss **cannot** match an eager PyTorch run, and "skip the
31	race's fwd/bwd and let the megakernel own fwd+bwd+opt" would train on gradients
32	unrelated to the task. (Three independent confirmations; see the cited file.)
33	
34	**What was built instead — the faithful unit.** The **L1 optimizer tail**
35	(`fused_optimizer_stage<Opt>`) reads the **real** gradient from global memory
36	(computed by the framework's own `loss.backward()`) and applies the canonical
37	per-element `apply_optimizer<Opt>` update. That is exactly the eager optimizer
38	step. So lever (a) is wired as: **keep the real PyTorch forward + backward, and
39	replace `optimizer.step()` with the L1 fused megakernel** (`opt_only=True`). This
40	is validated by **optimizer-equivalence** + a **grok smoke**, not by an (ill-
41	posed) L3-vs-eager loss test. The L3 path stays compiled (perf-placement
42	coverage) and reachable via `opt_only=False`, but is **not** the race path.
43	
44	---

219	## 7. Known risks / caveats
220	
221	* **fp32 only.** The L1 tail indexes raw `float` memory; `fused_optimizer_step`
222	  raises on non-fp32 params and `.contiguous()`-es param/grad. The race runs AMP
223	  off by default, so this holds. With AMP on, the fused path raises and the run
224	  degrades to eager (no silent corruption).
225	* **`fused_step` does NOT run `check_param_grad`** (that guard is on the per-op
226	  path). The Python driver enforces dtype/contiguity instead; do not call the raw
227	  `ops.fused_step` with a non-contiguous/half tensor.
228	* **Single `(bc1, bc2)` per call** is correct only because every race parameter
229	  steps together (one shared step counter). A caller that steps tensors at
230	  different counts must call `fused_step` per-tensor with that tensor's bc. This
231	  is asserted-by-construction in the race and documented loudly in
232	  `opt_components.cuh` / `dispatch.cpp`.
233	* **Persistent optimizer state is owned by the driver**, keyed by `id(param)` on
234	  the optimizer instance (`_fused_state_cache`). It is allocated once per param
235	  and never reallocated (reallocating would reset momentum and the run would not
236	  grok). It is NOT checkpointed by `optimizer.state_dict()` — a mid-run
237	  save/restore would lose the fused momentum. For a from-scratch race this is a
238	  non-issue; flagged for any resume-from-checkpoint use.
239	* **L3 remains compiled but unused by the race.** If a future change wants real
240	  fused fwd+bwd+opt, the model stages must be replaced with the real model graph
241	  (out of scope here) — `opt_only=False` currently runs the surrogate.
242	* **gfx942 host launch is 🟡** (no hipcc/MI300X in the implementing environment);
243	  the AMD cells were regenerated for ABI consistency but only the sm_90 path is
244	  exercised by this runbook.
245	* **Per-parameter launch cost (perf, not correctness).** The `fused_step` ABI is
246	  one parameter tensor per call (`n=numel`, `n_tasks=1`, `state≥3n`), so
247	  `fused_optimizer_step` launches ONE persistent megakernel per parameter (each a
248	  `#SMs`-CTA grid where a single CTA does the one-task work). For a model with
249	  dozens of small params this is many tiny launches — expected to be SLOWER per
250	  step than a multi-tensor fused optimizer, and the roofline number for the fused
251	  AdamW/Lion path should be read with that in mind (it is a correctness/wiring
252	  deliverable at this ABI, not a throughput win). A batched multi-tensor ABI
253	  (pack all params into one call with real per-tensor `sizes`/`offsets`) is the
254	  natural follow-up but is out of scope for lever (a).

258	## PHASE 1 — the TRUE L3 fused megakernel for `decoder × adamw` (real fwd+bwd+opt)
259	
260	> Supersedes §0's "L3 cannot match eager" **for the one cell
261	> `(transformer_decoder, adamw)` on sm_90 only**. Every OTHER cell's L3 path is
262	> still the element-local surrogate (§0 holds for them); they remain compiled and
263	> unused by the race. This section is what changed in PHASE 1 and how to validate
264	> it. Source-complete only — the implementing agent did NOT build and did NOT run
265	> any GPU work (tuning owns the GPU).
266	
267	### What PHASE 1 does
268	
269	Replaces the SURROGATE model stage with the **REAL transformer-decoder
270	forward+backward** inside the existing persistent megakernel, so that for the
271	`decoder × adamw` cell **`(decoder × adamw)` runs as ONE persistent kernel per
272	training step** — real model math, real optimizer math, **zero intermediate
273	kernel launches** (the owner rejected CUDA graphs; this is the chosen path).
274	Weights/state stay resident; the stages are separated only by in-kernel grid
275	barriers.
276	
277	The race's `train_adamw` loop now, for the decoder cell, calls
278	`_try_fused_train_step(...)` FIRST: if the L3-REAL kernel is available it runs the
279	whole step (fwd+bwd+adamw) and returns the loss, and the loop **skips its own
280	eager forward/backward/`optimizer.step()`**. Otherwise it falls back to the eager
281	fwd+bwd + the L1 fused optimizer tail (the pre-PHASE-1 path). `eval_every`
282	evaluation stays eager/unchanged.
283	
284	### Exact architecture transcribed (cites grokking_race_v2.py)
285	
286	`_raw_model` → `Transformer(nl=2, d=128, h=4, ntok=99, seq=4)` (seq hardcoded 4):
287	
288	| component | def | shape |
289	|---|---|---|
290	| `tok` | `nn.Embedding(99,128)` (:360) | [99,128] |
291	| `pos` | `nn.Embedding(4,128)` (:360) | [4,128] |
292	| 2× `DecoderBlock` | (:346) | |
293	| `attn` | `nn.MultiheadAttention(128,4,batch_first)` (:349), **causal** `triu(diag=1)` (:352) | in_proj [384,128]+[384], out_proj [128,128]+[128] |
294	| `n1,n2` | `nn.LayerNorm(128)` (:350), eps **1e-5** | [128]×2 each |
295	| `ff` | `Linear(128,512)→GELU→Linear(512,128)` (:351) | [512,128]+[512], [128,512]+[128] |
296	| post-LN | `x=n1(x+attn(x)); h=n2(x+ff(x))` (:354-355) | |
297	| `norm` | `nn.LayerNorm(128)` (:362) | [128]×2 |
298	| `out` | `nn.Linear(128,99)` (:362) | [99,128]+[99] |
299	| forward | `h=tok+pos; for l: h=l(h); return out(norm(h)[:,-1,:])` (:366-368) | **LAST token** |
300	| loss | `F.cross_entropy(logits, targets)` (:745) | mean over B |
301	
302	**30 parameter tensors, 422,755 total params.** Numerics pinned (each verified
303	against autograd in `tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py`): **GELU = exact erf** (the
304	surrogate's tanh approx is ~4e-4 off — wrong here); LayerNorm **eps=1e-5**;
305	attention scale **1/√32**, softmax with row-max subtraction; CE **mean over B** →
306	`dlogits=(softmax−onehot)/B`. `nn.MultiheadAttention` is transcribed bit-identical
307	(in_proj packs `[Wq;Wk;Wv]` row-blocks; verified `max|diff|==0`).
308	
309	### Stage / barrier layout (one persistent kernel)
310	
311	`csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_decoder_megakernel.cuh`, gridDim = #SMs (one CTA/SM),
312	256 threads/CTA. **Batch-parallel** (NOT the param-tensor work-steal queue — that
313	would vary the batch→CTA grouping and fp32 sums aren't associative):
314	
315	```
316	P0  each CTA zeroes its OWN grad-partial slice + loss slot
317	--- grid barrier B0 ---
318	P1  each CTA owns a FIXED contiguous batch slice (blockIdx.x); processes its
319	    samples ONE AT A TIME (CTA-cooperative), accumulating each sample's weight-
320	    grad into the CTA's partial with a SINGLE-OWNER-THREAD-PER-ELEMENT rule
321	    (no atomics → deterministic), and sums its slice's NLL (fp32)
322	--- grid barrier B1 ---
323	P2  deterministic cross-CTA reduce: sum partial[0..nCTA) in ASCENDING CTA index
324	    into the global grad (no float atomics; order fixed → reuses the work-steal
325	    queue to pick WHO reduces which tensor). Loss: fp64 ordered sum → loss/B → a
326	    device float the host reads back.
327	--- grid barrier B2 (sync_reset: also resets the queue for P3) ---
328	P3  the REAL apply_optimizer<AdamW> tail consumes the reduced grad in place
329	```
330	
331	Determinism: fixed batch→CTA grouping + fixed ascending-CTA reduction order; **no
332	float atomics** in the weight-grad reduce. The embedding `tok.weight` scatter maps
333	**thread→embedding column** and loops `(sample,position)` sequentially, so
334	colliding token ids (vocab 99) accumulate deterministically.
335	
336	### SMEM budget per CTA
337	
338	One sample, one layer live (the backward **recomputes** each layer's forward from
339	the cached layer input rather than caching every intermediate, so only one layer's
340	activations are live): `DecSampleSmem` ≈ **41.96 KB** — UNDER the 48 KB static-smem
341	cliff, so NO dynamic-smem opt-in and the occupancy≥1 launch guard
342	(`dynamicSMemBytes=0`) is unchanged.
343	
344	### Weight layout (ONE source of truth)
345	
346	`tests/hw/decoder_oracle.py::decoder_param_layout()` (asserted == the eager
347	`named_parameters()` order in the parity test) is the single source. The C++
348	device header `csrc/fused/sm_90/decoder_layout.cuh` is **GENERATED** from the same
349	table by `megakernel_codegen.py --decoder-layout` and **static-asserts the count
350	(30) and total (422755)** + an offset/size consistency fold — a mismatch fails the
351	**build**, never corrupts at dispatch. The Python wrapper
352	(`dispatch.py::_DECODER_TOTAL_ELEMS`) and dispatch.cpp (`kDecoderTotalElems`)
353	mirror the literal and cross-check `params.numel()` at the call site.
354	
355	### ABI (no `bindings.cpp` / `setup.py` edit; the owned-seam extension)
356	
357	The pybind `m.def("fused_step", ...)` arity is pinned in `bindings.cpp` (NOT
358	owned), so `fused_step`'s arity is unchanged. The token path is carried through the
359	EXISTING tensors, and the **behavior** is extended in `dispatch.cpp` (owned):
360	
361	* `input` = **int32** `[B*(kSeq+1)]` — tokens `[B*kSeq]` then targets `[B]`
362	  (`B = numel/(kSeq+1)`; S/vocab/d are compile-time).
363	* `params` = flat `[422755]` fp32; `state` = `[m|v|extra]` (`3*total`) **+ a
364	  trailing loss slot** the kernel writes the mean CE into (read back in Python).
365	* the **workspace** (`nCTA*total` grad partials + `nCTA` loss) is device scratch
366	  allocated in `dispatch.cpp` (keyed by device) — it never crosses the ABI.
367	* routing: `dispatch.cpp::fused_step` branches on
368	  `(model=="transformer_decoder" && optimizer=="adamw" && !opt_only)` →
369	  `mega_decoder_real_adamw` (an `extern` nvcc launcher; **the 33 generated
370	  surrogate cells are untouched, so no cell/table regeneration is forced and git
371	  stays generator-consistent**). dispatch.cpp is HOST-compiled, so all
372	  `<<<>>>`/device code lives in the new nvcc TU
373	  `csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_decoder_real_adamw.cu` (picked up by setup.py's
374	  `csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu` glob), reached via an `extern` decl using the existing
375	  mirror structs (same FQN/layout → mangling matches).
376	
377	Python: `dispatch.py::fused_train_step(model, opt, module, optimizer, tokens,
378	targets, ...)` packs the int32 input, owns the persistent flat-param + state
379	buffers, calls `ops.fused_step(..., opt_only=False)`, scatters the updated params
380	back, and returns the loss. The L3-REAL tier marker is `_FUSED_L3_REAL` +
381	`has_l3_real()` (sm_90-only).

355	    def __init__(self, d, h, seq_len=4):
356	        super().__init__()

367	        super().__init__()

370	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.out = nn.Linear(d, ntok)
371	        self.register_buffer('pos_ids', torch.arange(seq).unsqueeze(0))

389	class ViT(nn.Module):
390	    def __init__(self, p=97, patch_dim=49, num_patches=16, d=128, h=4, nl=2, grad_checkpoint=True):
391	        super().__init__()
392	        self.patch_proj = nn.Linear(patch_dim, d)
393	        self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, 1, d) * 0.02)
394	        self.pos = nn.Embedding(num_patches + 1, d)
395	        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([EncoderBlock(d, h) for _ in range(nl)])
396	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.out = nn.Linear(d, p)
397	        self.register_buffer('pos_ids', torch.arange(num_patches + 1).unsqueeze(0))
398	        self.grad_checkpoint = grad_checkpoint
399	    def forward(self, x):
400	        B = x.size(0); h = self.patch_proj(x)
401	        h = torch.cat([self.cls_token.expand(B, -1, -1), h], dim=1)
402	        h = h + self.pos(self.pos_ids)
403	        for l in self.layers: h = _maybe_checkpoint(l, h, self.grad_checkpoint)
404	        return self.out(self.norm(h[:, 0, :]))

407	class SelectiveSSMLayer(nn.Module):
408	    def __init__(self, d, state_dim=16, dt_rank=None, expand_factor=2):
409	        super().__init__()
410	        self.state_dim = state_dim; self.d_inner = d * expand_factor
411	        self.dt_rank = dt_rank or max(d // 16, 1)
412	        self.in_proj = nn.Linear(d, self.d_inner * 2, bias=False)
413	        self.conv1d = nn.Conv1d(self.d_inner, self.d_inner, kernel_size=3,
414	                                padding=1, groups=self.d_inner, bias=True)
415	        self.x_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, self.dt_rank + state_dim * 2, bias=False)
416	        self.dt_proj = nn.Linear(self.dt_rank, self.d_inner, bias=True)
417	        A = torch.arange(1, state_dim + 1, dtype=torch.float32)
418	        self.A_log = nn.Parameter(torch.log(A.unsqueeze(0).expand(self.d_inner, -1)))
419	        self.D = nn.Parameter(torch.ones(self.d_inner))
420	        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(self.d_inner, d, bias=False)
421	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d)
422	    def _selective_scan(self, x, dt, B, C):
423	        batch, L, _ = x.shape; A = -torch.exp(self.A_log); dt = F.softplus(dt)
424	        # Try CUDA kernel
425	        if x.is_cuda:
426	            try:
427	                from mamba_scan_ext import selective_scan_cuda
428	                return selective_scan_cuda(
429	                    x.contiguous(), dt.contiguous(),
430	                    B.contiguous(), C.contiguous(), A.contiguous()
431	                )
432	            except ImportError:
433	                pass
434	        # Python fallback
435	        h = torch.zeros(batch, self.d_inner, self.state_dim, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
436	        ys = []
437	        for t in range(L):
438	            dt_t = dt[:, t, :].unsqueeze(-1)
439	            h = torch.exp(dt_t * A.unsqueeze(0)) * h + (dt_t * B[:, t, :].unsqueeze(1)) * x[:, t, :].unsqueeze(-1)
440	            ys.append((h * C[:, t, :].unsqueeze(1)).sum(-1))
441	        return torch.stack(ys, dim=1)
442	    def forward(self, x):
443	        residual = x; xz = self.in_proj(x); x_main, z = xz.chunk(2, dim=-1)
444	        x_main = F.silu(self.conv1d(x_main.transpose(1, 2)).transpose(1, 2))
445	        x_dbc = self.x_proj(x_main)
446	        dt, B, C = x_dbc.split([self.dt_rank, self.state_dim, self.state_dim], dim=-1)
447	        y = self._selective_scan(x_main, self.dt_proj(dt), B, C)
448	        y = self.out_proj((y + x_main * self.D.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0)) * F.silu(z))
449	        return self.norm(y + residual)

451	class MambaModel(nn.Module):
452	    def __init__(self, p=97, ntok=99, seq_len=8, d=128, nl=2, grad_checkpoint=True):
453	        super().__init__()
454	        self.tok = nn.Embedding(ntok, d); self.pos = nn.Embedding(seq_len, d)
455	        self.layers = nn.ModuleList([SelectiveSSMLayer(d) for _ in range(nl)])
456	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.out = nn.Linear(d, p)
457	        self.register_buffer('pos_ids', torch.arange(seq_len).unsqueeze(0))
458	        self.grad_checkpoint = grad_checkpoint

461	        for l in self.layers: h = _maybe_checkpoint(l, h, self.grad_checkpoint)
462	        return self.out(self.norm(h[:, -1, :]))

3	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4	// Stage 6 — sm_90 L3 persistent-megakernel internals (§1.1–§1.4, §1.13, §1.14).
5	//
6	// This header is the **uniform scheduler + barrier substrate** that every
7	// generated L3 megakernel (csrc/fused/sm_90/*.cu) composes on top of the §3.4
8	// warp-specialization primitives (csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh).
9	// It defines ONLY the cross-CTA coordination machinery; the per-(model,
10	// optimizer) compute stages live in the generated TUs.
11	//
12	// The four pieces, all sm_90-real (compile-verified via
13	// scripts/compile_to_object.sh) and degrading to a correct fallback on older
14	// arches so the codegen matrix still builds:
15	//
16	//   §1.1  TaskQueue        — a single global atomic work counter that every
17	//                            persistent CTA pulls parameter-tensor indices
18	//                            from (the ThunderKittens-interpreter pattern).
19	//   §1.2  work-stealing     — there is NO static partition: an idle CTA simply
20	//                            keeps calling TaskQueue::next(), so a CTA that
21	//                            finishes its tensor early steals the next one.
22	//                            (atomicAdd on the shared counter IS the steal.)
23	//   §1.3  sm_id()           — reads %smid so the host can pin one persistent
24	//                            CTA per SM and keep that SM's optimizer-state
25	//                            slice L2-warm across the step.
26	//   §1.4  GridBarrier       — a hand-built arrive/wait grid barrier from two
27	//                            global atomics + a sense-reversing generation
28	//                            counter. Reusable, needs NO cooperative launch
29	//                            (so it scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap).
30	//
31	// §1.14 fences: acquire/release are placed EXPLICITLY and MINIMALLY — exactly
32	// one __threadfence() before the arrival publish and one acquire load after
33	// the release wait at the barrier, and one fence at the task hand-off. No loose
34	// fences (a loose fence here is both a correctness and a >10% perf footgun).
35	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
36	
37	#include "csrc/common/platform.h"
38	#include "csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/warp_specialize.cuh"
39	#include <cuda_runtime.h>

42	
43	// =========================================================================
44	//  §1.3  SM-pinning: read the streaming-multiprocessor id via %smid.
45	//
46	//  The host launches exactly gridDim.x == #SMs CTAs (one persistent CTA per
47	//  SM) and uses sm_id() inside the kernel to index that SM's resident slice
48	//  of optimizer state, so the slice stays warm in this SM's L2 partition for
49	//  the whole step. On pre-sm_90 the asm is still valid (%smid exists since
50	//  sm_20); the guard only exists to keep a host-compile of this header clean.
51	// =========================================================================
52	__device__ __forceinline__ unsigned sm_id() {
53	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__)
54	    unsigned id;
55	    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%smid;" : "=r"(id));
56	    return id;
57	#else
58	    return 0u;
59	#endif
60	}
61	
62	// =========================================================================
63	//  §1.1 / §1.2  TaskQueue — global work counter + work-stealing.
64	//
65	//  One int in global memory (`g_next_task`, zero-initialized by the host).
66	//  Every CTA runs:
67	//      for (int t = q.next(); t < n_tasks; t = q.next()) process(t);
68	//  next() does `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` — a CTA that drains its tensor
69	//  early just grabs the next index, so faster SMs steal work from the queue
70	//  with no static load-balancing (§1.2). The atomic is the ONLY synchronizer;
71	//  task bodies are independent (one parameter tensor each), so no fence is
72	//  needed on the *pull* — the fence belongs at the grid barrier between the
73	//  forward / backward / optimizer phases (§1.4), not on the per-task pull.
74	//
75	//  By convention ONE thread per CTA (the elected leader) pulls a task and
76	//  broadcasts it to the block via shared memory; `next_block()` packages that.
77	// =========================================================================
78	struct TaskQueue {
79	    int* g_next_task;   // global counter (host memset to 0 before launch)
80	    int  n_tasks;       // total parameter tensors to process this phase
81	
82	    __device__ __forceinline__ explicit TaskQueue(int* counter, int total)
83	        : g_next_task(counter), n_tasks(total) {}
84	
85	    // Per-thread atomic pull (used when every thread independently claims work,
86	    // e.g. a warp-granular schedule). Returns a task index that may be >=
87	    // n_tasks (caller bounds-checks).
88	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next() {
89	        return atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
90	    }
91	
92	    // Per-CTA pull: the leader thread does the single atomicAdd and broadcasts
93	    // the claimed index to the whole block through `smem_slot`. All threads in
94	    // the block then cooperate on that one tensor. Returns the claimed index.
95	    __device__ __forceinline__ int next_block(int* smem_slot) {
96	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
97	            *smem_slot = atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1);
98	        }
99	        __syncthreads();
100	        int t = *smem_slot;
101	        __syncthreads();   // ensure every thread read before slot is reused
102	        return t;
103	    }
104	};
105	
106	// =========================================================================
107	//  §1.4  GridBarrier — hand-built, reusable, sense-reversing grid barrier.
108	//
109	//  State (all in global memory, host-zero-initialized):
110	//    arrived    — count of CTAs that have reached the current barrier
111	//    generation — flips/advances each time the barrier is crossed (the "sense"
112	//                 a late CTA waits on so an early CTA can't lap it)
113	//
114	//  The classic correctness hazard with a counter barrier is *reuse*: if you
115	//  just reset `arrived` to 0, a fast CTA can enter the NEXT barrier and
116	//  increment the counter before a slow CTA has observed the release of the
117	//  PREVIOUS one. The sense-reversing generation fixes this: each CTA samples
118	//  the generation on entry, then waits until the generation has ADVANCED
119	//  (the last arriver advances it), never touching `arrived` for reset on the
120	//  consumer side. The last CTA to arrive resets `arrived` to 0 and bumps the
121	//  generation in one release; everyone else spins on the generation.
122	//
123	//  Fences (§1.14):
124	//    * The releasing writes a CTA makes BEFORE the barrier (its phase output)
125	//      must be visible to peers AFTER the barrier. We publish arrival with a
126	//      __threadfence() (device-scope release) before the atomicAdd, and the
127	//      waiters do an acquire by reading the generation with volatile semantics
128	//      and a __threadfence() after the wait completes. Exactly two fences per
129	//      CTA per barrier — the minimum for a correct release/acquire pair.
130	//
131	//  Only thread 0 of each CTA participates in the cross-CTA handshake; the rest
132	//  of the block is gated by a __syncthreads() so the whole CTA leaves together.
133	// =========================================================================
134	struct GridBarrier {
135	    unsigned* g_arrived;      // CTAs arrived at current phase
136	    unsigned* g_generation;   // sense-reversing generation counter
137	    unsigned  n_ctas;         // gridDim.x (CTAs that must arrive)
138	
139	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier(unsigned* arrived,
140	                                            unsigned* generation,
141	                                            unsigned grid_ctas)
142	        : g_arrived(arrived), g_generation(generation), n_ctas(grid_ctas) {}
143	
144	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync() const {
145	        // The block must fully reach the barrier before its leader publishes.
146	        __syncthreads();
147	
148	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
149	            // Sample the sense we are waiting to leave.
150	            unsigned my_gen =
151	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
152	
153	            // §1.14 RELEASE: make this CTA's phase writes visible device-wide
154	            // BEFORE we announce arrival, so a peer that observes our arrival
155	            // (and crosses) also observes our outputs.
156	            __threadfence();
157	
158	            // Atomically join the arrival count. The CTA whose add completes
159	            // the set (== n_ctas) is the "last arriver".
160	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
161	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
162	                // Last arriver: clear the count for the NEXT phase, then bump
163	                // the generation. Order matters — reset arrived to 0 first,
164	                // then a release-store of the advanced generation so a CTA that
165	                // sees the new generation also sees arrived==0 when it next
166	                // enters. atomicExch gives the store device-scope visibility.
167	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
168	                __threadfence();
169	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
170	            } else {
171	                // Not last: spin until the generation advances past our sample.
172	                // §1.14b BACKOFF: a tight volatile-read spin hammers the L2 /
173	                // memory subsystem with the generation poll and steals issue
174	                // slots from arriving CTAs. __nanosleep parks the spinning warp
175	                // for an exponentially-growing nap (capped) so the poll rate
176	                // drops and the memory subsystem is left to the laggard CTAs.
177	                // Behavior-preserving: still exits the instant the generation
178	                // advances; only the *poll cadence* changes (sm_70+; on older
179	                // arches the asm is a no-op fallback).
180	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
181	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
182	                       == my_gen) {
183	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
184	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
185	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
186	#endif
187	                }
188	            }
189	
190	            // §1.14 ACQUIRE: after observing the generation advance, fence so
191	            // the peers' phase writes (released above) are visible to us.
192	            __threadfence();
193	        }
194	
195	        // Release the rest of the block once the leader has crossed.
196	        __syncthreads();
197	    }
198	
199	    // #4 — barrier with a FUSED task-counter reset. The L3 phase loop used to do
200	    //   fwd → sync → reset_counter → sync → bwd → sync → reset_counter → sync
201	    // (4 grid barriers + 2 standalone in-kernel counter resets). The reset is
202	    // folded into THIS barrier's last-arriver critical section: the last CTA
203	    // zeroes `*reset_counter` BEFORE the release-store that advances the
204	    // generation, so any CTA that later observes the new generation (and thus
205	    // crosses) is guaranteed to see the counter == 0 for the next phase. That
206	    // removes the two standalone resets AND their two barriers — 4 → 2 grid
207	    // barriers per L3 step — with identical phase ordering/visibility. Pass the
208	    // task-queue counter (ctx.g_next_task) as `reset_counter`.
209	    __device__ __forceinline__ void sync_reset(int* reset_counter) const {
210	        __syncthreads();
211	
212	        if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
213	            unsigned my_gen =
214	                *reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation);
215	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 RELEASE: publish phase writes before arrival.
216	            unsigned prev = atomicAdd(g_arrived, 1u);
217	            if (prev + 1u == n_ctas) {
218	                // Last arriver: clear arrival count AND reset the task counter
219	                // for the next phase, then a release-store of the advanced
220	                // generation. Ordering: both resets, then __threadfence(), then
221	                // the generation bump — so observers of the new gen see both
222	                // arrived==0 and reset_counter==0.
223	                atomicExch(g_arrived, 0u);
224	                atomicExch(reinterpret_cast<unsigned*>(reset_counter), 0u);
225	                __threadfence();
226	                atomicAdd(g_generation, 1u);
227	            } else {
228	                unsigned backoff = 32u;
229	                while (*reinterpret_cast<volatile unsigned*>(g_generation)
230	                       == my_gen) {
231	#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && (__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 700)
232	                    __nanosleep(backoff);
233	                    backoff = (backoff < 1024u) ? (backoff << 1) : 1024u;
234	#endif
235	                }
236	            }
237	            __threadfence();   // §1.14 ACQUIRE.
238	        }
239	
240	        __syncthreads();
241	    }
242	};

244	// =========================================================================
245	//  PersistentContext — the bundle of global scratch a generated L3 megakernel
246	//  needs. The host allocates these (all zero-initialized) and passes their
247	//  device pointers to the kernel. Grouping them keeps the generated kernel
248	//  signatures uniform across all 99 cells.
249	// =========================================================================
250	struct PersistentContext {
251	    int*      g_next_task;     // §1.1 TaskQueue counter
252	    unsigned* g_arrived;       // §1.4 GridBarrier arrival count
253	    unsigned* g_generation;    // §1.4 GridBarrier generation
254	    int       n_tasks;         // parameter tensors this step
255	    unsigned  n_ctas;          // persistent CTAs (== #SMs, one per SM, §1.3)
256	
257	    __device__ __forceinline__ TaskQueue queue() const {
258	        return TaskQueue(g_next_task, n_tasks);
259	    }
260	    __device__ __forceinline__ GridBarrier barrier() const {
261	        return GridBarrier(g_arrived, g_generation, n_ctas);
262	    }
263	};
264	
265	}} // namespace sg::fused

class EncoderBlock(nn.Module):

        super().__init__()

        self.n1 = nn.LayerNorm(d); self.n2 = nn.LayerNorm(d)

class ViT(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, p=97, patch_dim=49, num_patches=16, d=128, h=4, nl=2):

    out  = nn.Linear(128, 97)              # :396  head → 97 logits (== p)
    forward: h = patch_proj(x)                          # :400  [B,16,d]

  * CrossEntropy is MEAN over B: dlogits = (softmax - onehot) / B.
